decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: The recognizable international stems follow the bounded borrowing policy and occur alongside an attested number headword. OLP-0007 fixes their basic scope. OLP-0043 constructs each rational as an equivalence class of integer pairs with nonzero second coordinate, defines arithmetic and order on representatives, and embeds each integer as the class of its pair with 1. These exact sets and operations come from the source definitions and formulas rather than the canon; no native Javanese foundations attestation is claimed.

decisions.english_term_or_issue: numbers or relations are sets, metaphysically speaking; treat them as sets; embed their theories
decisions.chosen_javanese: wilangan utawa relasi iku himpunan saka sisi metafisika; nganggep wilangan utawa relasi minangka himpunan; nyisipake teori-teorine
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0013 distinguishes a metaphysical identity assertion from the weaker mathematical practice of treating certain relations as sets. OLP-0046 makes the parallel distinction for numbers: alternative ordered-pair implementations produce different set objects, natural zero is not literally the constructed integer zero, and the warranted conclusion is only that set theory lets us treat the numbers as sets and embed their theories. OLP-0053 adds that any Dedekind algebra exemplifies the desired natural-number structure and that all such algebras are isomorphic, while expressly withholding an answer about which objects are the natural numbers; the embedding is also conditional on a Dedekind-infinite set. General relasi, wilangan, konteks, and teori have canon support, while no Javanese canon source is claimed to settle the philosophy of mathematics.

decisions.chosen_javanese: rerangken Cauchy; nyedhaki nol; limit
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0048 defines a Cauchy sequence as a function from Nat to Rat whose values become pairwise epsilon-close beyond some natural bound, and defines tending to zero by the corresponding absolute-value condition. The canon supports orthography, general function and number language and scholarly register, but no specialized native analysis attestation is claimed.

decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0051 defines X as f-closed exactly when every f(x) for x in X remains in X, and defines the closure of o as the intersection of all such sets containing o. OLP-0054 generalizes from one generator to a subset and uses that closure in the Schröder-Bernstein sandwich proof; JV-D064 states the corresponding self-map and carrier-subset scope needed by the generalized definition and lemma. Tutupan and katutup transparently distinguish the generated object from the preservation property; the canon supports general function, member and scholarly-definition language but does not attest this specialist closure terminology.

decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0063 titles the shared first-order/propositional wrapper and gives its reuse guidance. OLP-0064 defines a derivation as a finite syntactic object and an axiomatic derivation by fixed axioms or inference rules. OLP-0087 uses bisa diderivasi for the sentencehood consequence of the quantifier-elimination rules, preserving an explicit proof-theoretic relation instead of generic production. OLP-0088 gives the inductive and finite-tree definitions of a natural-deduction derivation and ties bisa diderivasi exactly to existence of such a tree from Gamma. OLP-0089 applies the same derivability vocabulary to each constructed disjunction branch and reaffirms that a lone assumption is itself a base-case derivation. OLP-0090 uses bisa diderivasi for quantified goals and contradictions and distinguishes formal derivation from generic production throughout the worked examples. Retain derivasi and the adapted proof-theory vocabulary under the borrowing policy; canon does not attest the complete compounds. OLP-0091 defines bisa diderivasi saka by a derivation whose conclusion is A and whose assumptions are discharged or belong to Gamma, then reuses that exact relation throughout the structural properties. OLP-0092 composes exact derivations of A and falsum, preserving their open assumption sets, negation inferences and resulting derivability claims. OLP-0093 preserves the exact conjunction, disjunction and conditional derivations, their premise order and every resulting formula. OLP-0094 preserves a named derivation of A(c) and the two one-step quantifier derivations with their exact premise and conclusion order. OLP-0095 analyzes eight exact proof trees and the remaining rule cases, preserving each premise derivation, conclusion and rule direction. OLP-0096 preserves identity introduction, both identity-elimination directions and four exact natural-deduction trees. OLP-0097 verifies the exact identity-elimination proof tree and keeps each premise derivation and conclusion in order. OLP-0099 states that every non-assumption signed formula results from an inference rule applied to an earlier formula on the same branch. OLP-0100 presents the eight connective inference rules and the optional Cut rule through exact signed-formula displays. OLP-0101 presents four signed quantifier inference rules, their side conditions and the substitution form of False existential. OLP-0102 defines every non-assumption tableau entry as the result of a correct inference-rule application to an entry above it on the same branch. OLP-0103 applies the signed connective inference rules step by step, preserving each source line, result line and rule label. OLP-0104 records every quantified and propositional inference rule beside its exact source line and resulting signed formula. OLP-0105 defines bisa diderivasi saka through a finite premise subset and a closed tableau for the false target together with the true premises. OLP-0106 uses Proves and bisa diderivasi through closed tableaux with exact finite signed premise sets, including both directions of the negation conversion. OLP-0107 uses bisa diderivasi for conjunction projections and pairing, disjunction injections, modus ponens and two conditional claims. OLP-0108 preserves a closed tableau for A(c), its converted universal witness and the two quantified instance derivability relations. OLP-0109 checks every nonsplitting and splitting tableau rule family, including the quantified cases and Cut, as a satisfiability-preserving expansion. OLP-0110 adds three exact identity inference rules to the tableau system and keeps both prerequisite formulas explicit for each signed replacement. OLP-0111 checks the reflexive and true identity rules explicitly and identifies the false-signed identity case as the exact dual. OLP-0112 assembles the complete axiomatic derivation chapter from its exact rule, proof, provability, soundness and identity imports. OLP-0113 defines the axiomatic derivation system, inference rules and derivability relation through the exact finite-sequence conditions. OLP-0114 defines the propositional axiom set and states modus ponens as the rule licensing A from earlier B and B implies A. OLP-0115 states the two quantified axioms and the two conditional inference rules while preserving each rule's exact direction and freshness condition. OLP-0116 follows each derivable target through its exact axiom instances and modus-ponens steps, including the Gamma-relative chain example. OLP-0117 uses the derivable predicate for each exact chained implication and then applies the quantified rule to the final universally quantified target. OLP-0118 fixes axiomatic derivability and theoremhood by the final formula of a derivation, then proves reflexivity, monotonicity and transitivity.

Retain the source term soundness with the descriptive gloss jaminan semantis so it cannot collapse into ordinary validity; OLP-0068 consequently renders a sound and complete system as one that ngemu jaminan semantis lan jangkep rather than reusing sah. OLP-0072 spells out the same soundness condition directly as the system deriving only valid sequents, again avoiding ordinary sah. Kelengkapan and validitas remain recognizable provisional adaptations because canon does not attest the metatheoretic terms. OLP-0091 states that soundness and completeness establish the mutual correspondence between the semantic and proof-theoretic notions, replacing a bare-sameness wording while preserving the theorem names. OLP-0095 states soundness as derivability from open assumptions implying semantic entailment and derives validity and consistency consequences. OLP-0105 states that soundness and completeness establish the mutual correspondence between semantic and tableau proof-theoretic notions, using cocog siji lan sijine rather than literal identity. OLP-0109 states tableau soundness as closed tableau implying unsatisfiability and derives validity, semantic consequence and consistency in that direction. OLP-0111 extends tableau soundness to identity by proving that no satisfiable closed tableau can result from any identity-rule expansion. OLP-0118 states that soundness and completeness together establish the correspondence between semantic and proof-theoretic notions.

OLP-0106 applies ora konsisten to four exact tableau claims: contraction, the two provability equivalences, explicit inconsistency and exhaustive cases. OLP-0107 states that a disjunction with the negations of both disjuncts is ora konsisten and supplies the exact closed tableau witness. OLP-0109 proves by contrapositive that satisfiability implies consistency, using a finite closed-tableau witness for inconsistency. OLP-0118 defines axiomatic consistency through non-derivability of false and records the equivalent explosion characterization.
